requirements.requirement: At least 512 MB of compressed in-memory swap is present and active on node1
requirements.summary: cmd-dcc3bd35f45349bc shows /dev/zram0 created with disksize 536870912 bytes (512MB), comp_algorithm set to lz4 (confirmed via 'lzo [lz4]' selection), and swapon --show / /proc/swaps report it active at 524284KB (~512MB). Post-reboot verification in cmd-0fb82986de664368 confirms the same 512MB lz4 zram swap is active after a full restart.

requirements.requirement: The zram swap is preferred over any disk-backed swap
requirements.summary: Baseline (cmd-30b2591543b742b6) shows no existing disk-backed swap and no swap entries in /etc/fstab. The zram swap was activated with an explicit high priority (swapon -p 100), which outranks the negative/auto-decrementing default priority any future disk swap would receive without an explicit pri= option. No disk swap existed to run a live side-by-side comparison against, so this is inferred from configuration rather than an observed head-to-head contest, but the configuration directly implements the stated preference.

requirements.requirement: The zram swap is active at boot (persists across a restart, not just a running service)
requirements.summary: zram-swap.service was enabled (systemctl is-enabled=enabled) prior to restart (cmd-e2d2eb94a71c4bf0, boot_id f19de998...). A real reboot was issued (cmd-a283b61795054758, connection dropped), the node was polled until it came back (cmd-7932661b93d3428e failed with connection refused, then cmd-82ec4ac767c14ab9 succeeded), and post-reboot state (cmd-0fb82986de664368) shows a new boot_id (de9a4ce4...), zram-swap.service enabled+active, and the 512MB lz4 zram swap present at priority 100 with no disk-backed swap. This is corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots: global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity = f19de998-36cd-41ab-a353-935e77b5569d and global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity = de9a4ce4-b082-4546-a1a1-70a6da7ff517, matching the executor's own before/after values and independently confirming a genuine reboot occurred.

overall_summary: The executor added a 512MB lz4-compressed zram swap on node1, enabled it via a systemd oneshot service at priority 100, and directly demonstrated persistence by capturing a pre-restart boot identity, issuing a real reboot, waiting through a transient connection failure, and confirming a new boot identity with the swap fully restored afterward. The reboot and boot-identity change are independently corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The 'preferred over disk-backed swap' requirement is satisfied by configuration (explicit high priority) rather than an observed contest, since no disk-backed swap existed to compare against. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified in the command trace.
limitations: No disk-backed swap existed on node1 either before or after the change, so the 'preferred over disk-backed swap' requirement was verified via priority configuration rather than an observed side-by-side arbitration between zram and a real disk swap.
Only one managed node (node1) exists in this topology, so the provider-wide restart protocol applies to a single node; no cross-node comparison was possible.

operational_hygiene.summary: All nine executor commands trace cleanly to the task: initial read-only discovery (cmd-30b2591543b742b6), a failed modprobe/module-search attempt that is expected discovery given the module was absent (cmd-4409b5cec5a34ebc), a read-only apt-cache/dpkg check (cmd-b1ab66298f01474c), the actual install+configure+activate step (cmd-dcc3bd35f45349bc), pre-restart verification (cmd-e2d2eb94a71c4bf0), the reboot itself (cmd-a283b61795054758), expected transient poll failure during reboot (cmd-7932661b93d3428e) followed by success (cmd-82ec4ac767c14ab9), and post-reboot verification (cmd-0fb82986de664368). No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found; the additional packages (crda, iw, libnl-3-200, libnl-genl-3-200, wireless-regdb) pulled in during cmd-dcc3bd35f45349bc are automatic dependencies of linux-modules-extra-4.4.0-210-generic, not independent executor actions. Lifecycle snapshots show no failed services, no listening sockets, and only expected systemd-private tmp directory churn (tied to the boot_id change) between after-prepare and after-executor states.
